title: China-to-Bosnia and Herzegovina EV Charger Compliance Gap Matrix
target_market: Bosnia and Herzegovina (BAS / DERK / NOS BiH)
provenance: AI-compiled, multi-model cross-checked, not human-verified. Informational only; confirm with the official regulator and a qualified professional. Not legal/certification/customs/market-access advice.

rows.requirement: Connector Redesign — GB/T 20234 versus IEC 62196 Type 2 and CCS2
rows.target_requirement: Bosnia and Herzegovina deployments in Europe-facing public and private charging are primarily built on IEC connector ecosystems. IEC 62196 Type 2 is used for AC charging and CCS2 for DC fast charging where specified by the buyer, operator, project, or vehicle fleet. Connector selection is a technical interoperability and procurement requirement, not legal approval for the whole unit.
target_standards: IEC 62196-3:2022 CCS Combo 2 / configuration FF ecosystem
Project, fleet, operator, or procurement connector requirements
rows.china_equivalent: China commonly uses GB/T 20234.2 for AC charging connection devices and GB/T 20234.3 for DC charging interfaces. GB/T 27930 is commonly used for charger-to-BMS communication. GB/T hardware and signalling should not be presented as Type 2 or CCS2 compliance without connector, cable, locking, pilot, communication, label, and safety re-evaluation.
rows.gap: GB/T-only chargers for Bosnia-facing projects need hardware and protocol conversion planning: Type 2 or CCS2 couplers, cable thermal rating, lock and proximity circuits, control-pilot behaviour, DC PLC where CCS2 is used, updated charger labels, spare-part lists, and retesting after connector redesign.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory where Bosnia project, procurement document, charging network, or fleet specifies Type 2 / CCS2 operation profile; otherwise a market-interoperability expectation rather than standalone legal approval
mandatory_status.cn: GB/T 20234 compliance is a China-market connector baseline and not a substitute for Type 2 or CCS2 compatibility

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Do not describe a GB/T 20234 package as Bosnia Type 2 or CCS2 ready. Prepare connector hardware, signalling, labels, and safety evidence around the specified IEC interface for the intended deployment.

rows.requirement: Grid-Connection and Project Acceptance for Bosnia EV Chargers
rows.target_requirement: Bosnia and Herzegovina charging stations intended for grid connection must still pass project and NOS BiH route acceptance. For public or semi-public charging, requirements can include station registration, metering and tariff data, grid interconnection drawings, protection and earthing assumptions, and commissioning records. Product certificates alone are not project acceptance in Bosnia.
target_standards: Bosnia and Herzegovina energy installation and charger project practices
DERK and NOS BiH grid operator acceptance route
Distribution-company interconnection and local installation requirements
rows.china_equivalent: China GB/T 18487.1 and related station documentation support technical comparison for equipment readiness. However, Chinese project paperwork does not establish Bosnia station registration, DERK governance alignment, or NOS BiH acceptance by itself.
rows.gap: Prepare Bosnia-ready station documents for each site: electrical single-line diagrams, interconnection permission, metering and tariff references, station owner/operator identification, commissioning protocol, and operator or fleet integration evidence aligned to DERK and NOS BiH expectations.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory where project grid interconnection and acceptance is required for the Bosnia site and public or fleet operation
mandatory_status.cn: China project files do not establish Bosnia grid-connection or station registration rights

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] A CE or GB/T charger file alone is insufficient for Bosnia grid acceptance. Confirm station registration, metering, and commissioning steps with the local operator and DERK for each location.

source.publisher: Independent System Operator of Bosnia and Herzegovina (NOS BiH)

rows.requirement: Bosnia Market Authorization and CE-Aligned Technical Documentation
rows.target_requirement: Bosnia-facing EV chargers should be prepared with market-facing technical documentation and declarations for applicable EU-aligned product legislation and operator requirements. IEC 61851-1:2017 is the core conductive charging safety standard for EV supply equipment and is used to define electrical safety, EVSE-to-vehicle interface conditions, and operational states within project-ready technical packs.
target_standards: CE marking for applicable EU-aligned product legislation
BAS and project-level EN/IEC electrical acceptance references
rows.china_equivalent: China files commonly use GB/T 18487.1 and GB/T 20234 references for conductive charging requirements. These are useful for clause mapping but do not replace Bosnia-facing CE-aligned technical files, declarations, local manual language, or market-route approvals.
rows.gap: The gap is that technical files should be converted to Bosnia-facing structure: applicable directives, harmonized or adopted standard list, test reports, critical component certificates, risk analysis, local language manuals and warnings, declaration of conformity, label artwork, and change-control evidence.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory where the charger falls under applicable CE-aligned product law and project procurement requires Bosnia-facing technical documentation
mandatory_status.cn: China GB/T baseline does not constitute Bosnia market authorization without Bosnia conversion

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Treat IEC / EN evidence as part of a Bosnia-ready CE technical-file route, not as a standalone market approval. Confirm the exact market route and local approval model before claiming readiness.

source.publisher: Institute for Standardization of Bosnia and Herzegovina (BAS)

rows.target_requirement: Bosnia projects may require OCPP for backend interoperability and separate evidence for EU-aligned electrical safety, including EMC and residual-current-protection design. OCPP 1.6, OCPP 2.0.1, and OCPP 2.1 versions may be used depending on operator and procurement scope, with security profile and backend integration requirements to be specified per station contract.
target_standards: Relevant Bosnia and Herzegovina grid-side and station protection requirements
rows.china_equivalent: China-market DC chargers commonly rely on GB/T 27930 for charger-to-vehicle battery-management communication. That protocol is not operator backend protocol and does not replace OCPP, station cybersecurity, backend acceptance testing, or firmware-management procedures required by Bosnia projects.
rows.gap: Bosnia deployment files should identify exact OCPP version, security profile, certificate handling, meter-value mapping, transaction model, remote reset and firmware update process, interface architecture, and test evidence from the target charging management system.

mandatory_status.target: Usually mandatory when required by operator, tender, roaming, payment, or maintenance specification; OCPP and EMC evidence are not standalone whole-unit safety certification
mandatory_status.cn: GB/T 27930 is vehicle-side communication and does not satisfy OCPP backend or Bosnia operator interoperability requirements

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Confirm OCPP version and security profile with the Bosnia operator before shipment and define EMC/RCD implementation for the target deployment route.

rows.requirement: EMC, Low-Voltage Safety, and Residual-Current Protection
rows.target_requirement: EV chargers in Bosnia and Herzegovina can require conformity evidence for applicable electrical safety and electromagnetic compatibility rules. For EVSE, IEC 61851-1 includes EVSE electrical safety requirements, while EMC evidence is mapped to charger-specific EMC routes and Bosnia-relevant installation practices. Residual-current protection, DC residual-current detection, protective earthing, overcurrent and surge protection, and site coordination should be documented for the final deployment.
target_standards: Directive 2014/35/EU Low Voltage Directive, Bosnia-aligned implementation to be verified
Directive 2014/30/EU EMC Directive, Bosnia-aligned implementation to be verified
IEC 61851-21-2 EMC route for off-board EV charging systems, current edition to be verified
rows.china_equivalent: China files may include GB/T 18487.1 safety evidence, GB/T 18487.2 EMC evidence for off-board conductive supply equipment, component certificates, and site electrical drawings. These should be mapped by clause and retested where needed for Bosnia-compatible EN/IEC, site-earthing, RCD, and installation assumptions.
rows.gap: The gap is often installation assumptions rather than only lab reports: earthing system, upstream breaker, RCD or RDC-DD arrangement, DC leakage handling, EMC cable routing, surge protection, short-circuit rating, enclosure IP/IK, ambient rating, and local language warnings should match the actual deployment.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory where Bosnia-aligned low-voltage and EMC obligations apply; residual-current and installation protection are mandatory where required by local design, grid connection, and electrical code route
mandatory_status.cn: China GB/T safety and EMC evidence supports comparison but does not replace Bosnia CE and site-installation verification

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Do not rely on China lab reports without checking Bosnia route and Bosnia-compatible protection assumptions. Validate RCD, earthing, leakage handling, EMC design, and commissioning controls before energization.
